title: The Greek World
questions: What does Achilles want, and does he get it?
How do the tragedians treat the conflict between family obligation and the law of the city?
Thucydides and Plato both lived through the Peloponnesian War. What did each conclude from it?
How does Aristotle's account of the good life differ from Plato's?

works.author: Homer
works.title: The Iliad
works.focus: Iliad first. Mark Book 9 (the embassy), Book 18 (the shield), and Book 24 (Priam and Achilles). Then the Odyssey, tracking hospitality and homecoming.
works.edition: Iliad tr. Richmond Lattimore (Chicago) or Robert Fagles (Penguin); Odyssey tr. Lattimore (Harper) or Emily Wilson (Norton)

works.author: Hesiod
works.title: Theogony
works.focus: Theogony for the genealogy of the gods; Works and Days for the ethic of labor and justice.
works.edition: Tr. M.L. West, Theogony and Works and Days (Oxford World's Classics)

works.author: Aeschylus
works.title: The Oresteia
works.focus: Read the Oresteia as one trilogy. The Eumenides ends a cycle of vengeance with a court at Athens.
works.edition: Tr. Richmond Lattimore, in The Complete Greek Tragedies (Chicago); or tr. Robert Fagles (Penguin)

works.author: Sophocles
works.title: The Theban Plays
works.focus: Oedipus the King, Oedipus at Colonus, Antigone. Antigone sets divine law against the decree of the city.
works.edition: Tr. Robert Fagles, The Three Theban Plays (Penguin); or David Grene, Sophocles I (Chicago)

works.author: Euripides
works.title: The Tragedies
works.focus: Medea, Hippolytus, The Trojan Women, The Bacchae.
works.edition: The Complete Greek Tragedies: Euripides, ed. Grene and Lattimore (Chicago)

works.author: Aristophanes
works.title: The Comedies
works.focus: The Clouds first; its caricature of Socrates is the counterpart to Plato's portrait. Then The Frogs and Lysistrata.
works.edition: Tr. Peter Meineck, Clouds (Hackett); or Alan Sommerstein, Lysistrata and Other Plays (Penguin)

works.author: Herodotus
works.title: The Histories
works.focus: Books I-II for method and digression, VII-IX for the Persian invasion.
works.edition: The Landmark Herodotus, ed. Robert Strassler, tr. Andrea Purvis (Anchor)

works.author: Thucydides
works.title: The Peloponnesian War
works.focus: Pericles' Funeral Oration (II.35-46), the plague (II.47-54), the Mytilenean debate (III.36-50), the Melian dialogue (V.84-116), the Sicilian expedition (VI-VII).
works.edition: The Landmark Thucydides, ed. Robert Strassler, tr. Richard Crawley (Free Press)

works.title: The Pre-Socratics
works.focus: Heraclitus and Parmenides above all; the problem of change and permanence sets up Plato.
works.edition: Ed. and tr. Jonathan Barnes, Early Greek Philosophy (Penguin); or Kirk, Raven and Schofield, The Presocratic Philosophers (Cambridge)

works.author: Plato
works.title: Republic
works.focus: Suggested order: Gorgias, Phaedo, Symposium, Republic, Phaedrus, Timaeus. Leave the Laws for a later pass. The Apology and Crito, though not listed, are a short useful preface.
works.edition: Plato: Complete Works, ed. John M. Cooper (Hackett). Republic tr. Allan Bloom (Basic Books) or Grube/Reeve (Hackett)

works.author: Aristotle
works.title: Nicomachean Ethics
works.focus: Nicomachean Ethics in full; then Politics I-III, Poetics, On the Soul II-III, Physics II, Metaphysics I and XII.
works.edition: Nicomachean Ethics tr. Terence Irwin (Hackett) or Bartlett and Collins (Chicago); Politics tr. C.D.C. Reeve (Hackett); Poetics tr. Joe Sachs (Focus)
